chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“When you reach a man at the time of the death-throes, then prompt him with the words of relief: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous; there is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent; Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is in them and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
“And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

He said: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said, “If I had reached ʿIkrimah at the time of death, I would have benefited him.” So it was said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “By what would he have benefited him?” He said, “He would have prompted him with that which you are upon.”

key_terms.النَّزْعِ: the final agonies or death-throes at the approach of death
key_terms.الْحَلِيمُ: the Forbearing, one of the divine attributes mentioned in the formula
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, referring to Allah’s mighty Throne
key_terms.الْعَلِيُّ: the Most High, one of the divine attributes mentioned in the formula
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death, the moment when this prompting is to occur
key_terms.فَلَقِّنْهُ: prompt him to recite or repeat words at death
key_terms.كَلِمَاتِ الْفَرَجِ: the phrases of relief recited for ease and deliverance
key_terms.مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ: that which you are upon, meaning the belief or doctrine held by the addressed followers

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a person at the time of death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that a dying person should be prompted with specific words of tawhid, glorification, and praise of Allah. It also indicates that affirming the truth held by the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام at the moment of death is of benefit to the dying person.
